Subject: Initial ask: multi-year commitment structure and payment terms

Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team was impressed with the latency numbers for long-context retrievals. We're ready to discuss a multi-year commitment, but procurement has strict payment rules. A few constraints: 1) they prefer Net90 on enterprise contracts, 2) they require staged payments tied to delivery milestones, and 3) they can only approve up to 40% upfront as a deposit unless there's a clear ramp schedule.

Could you share a proposed payment ladder (deposit / milestones / annual billing) and confirm whether Redwood can make a Net90 exception in exchange for a larger upfront deposit or an escrow arrangement? Also attaching a draft SOW for context.

Best,

Erin —

Appreciate the clear constraints. High-level proposal attached; summary below so it's easy for procurement:

- Term: 3 years committed (annual volumes locked)
- Pricing: step discount: year1 list -10%, year2 -15%, year3 -18% off list (volume tiers baked into SOW)
- Payment ladder (proposal): 40% deposit at signing; 30% at end of Q2 (after onboarding + first integration milestone); remaining 30% split across annual invoices (yearly in arrears)
- Net terms: We can consider Net90 on the annual invoices only (not deposit) if Skyline agrees to an escrow holding for the deposit or an increased deposit to 50% for Year1.
- Other asks: early termination fees scale with prepayment; we propose prorated credits if term changes.

I've looped Lauren (solutions) and Ben (finance lead) to vet the billing side. Attached: Redwood_Terms_Net90_Request.docx with two Net90 variants (escrow vs increased deposit).

Next step: would procurement be open to 50% deposit + escrow for the deposit, or do they need to keep deposit at 40%? If 40% is fixed, we can push for a shorter Net (Net60) or require additional collateral.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

Jonas/Erin —

Procurement here. Our policy is firm on Net90 for software vendors unless there is a formal waiver. Typical waivers we grant are limited to: escrow for deposits, third-party guarantee, or pre-approved vendor credit lines. The maximum upfront deposit we can approve without additional approvals is 40%. Increasing to 50% will require executive sign-off and justification.

If Redwood can accept 40% deposit + escrow and provide milestone-based release terms (i.e., release X% after onboarding, Y% after pilot acceptance), we can route expeditiously. Otherwise, we'll need to involve legal and finance and that will add another 2-3 weeks.

Tom from CC Partners is copied to advise on procurement-side precedent.

Procurement Team
Skyline Health

Lauren —

Finance ran the numbers. Trade-off options:
1) 40% escrow + milestone release: we can offer an additional 2% up-front discount (effectively year1 -12% overall) and hold list discounts for years 2/3 as proposed. This keeps cash exposure manageable and preserves revenue recognition certainty.
2) If Skyline pushes for 50% deposit (no escrow), we can push to year1 -15% but this requires CFO sign-off and a 30-day lead time.

Recommendation: propose option #1 to Skyline (escrow + milestone release + Net60 on annual invoices), and indicate flexibility to move to Net90 if legal signs a limited waiver and execs approve a 50% deposit.

Ben Carter
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Final proposal: escrowed deposit + milestone ladder + conditional Net90

Erin / Procurement team —

Thanks for the patience while we evaluated the options internally. Final proposal (so procurement has a single doc to review):

1) Term & Pricing: 3-year commitment with stepped discounts: Year1 -12% effective, Year2 -15%, Year3 -18% (volume bands in SOW).

2) Deposit & Escrow: 40% deposit at signing to a mutually-agreed escrow. Escrow release schedule: 20% on completion of onboarding checklist, 10% on pilot acceptance, 10% on GA/production launch. Redwood and Skyline will sign a short Escrow Release Addendum outlining release triggers.

3) Net terms: Redwood will accept Net60 on annual invoices by default. Net90 may be granted for annual invoices only if Skyline signs the Escrow Addendum and completes internal waiver form (Procurement_Waiver_Form.pdf). In the event Skyline secures executive approval for a 50% deposit (no escrow), Redwood will accept Net90 on all invoices for Year1 and Year2.

4) Termination & Credits: If Skyline terminates for convenience in Year1, Redwood will apply prorated credits against unused prepaid deposit per the SOW schedule. No refunds until milestone releases are processed in escrow.

Next steps: if Procurement agrees to the escrow + Net60 path, we can circulate a redline SOW and an Escrow Addendum for signatures and aim to start onboarding within 4 weeks. If they require Net90 without escrow, we'll need an exec-level waiver and a follow-up call to finalize.

Erin — happy to hop on a quick call with Tom from CC Partners if that helps expedite.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
